tools.name: Groq Playground
tools.skill: Use a hosted model to classify feedback, then score it against your own labels.
tools.setup: Create your own Groq account. Open the Playground and select a currently available free-tier text model. A key is needed only if you move to the API.
tools.assignment: Label the fictional reviews yourself before running the prompt. Compare the output to your labels, rerun one ambiguous case with a clearer definition, and report the disagreement.
tools.caution: Model choice and quotas change. Do not enable paid billing for this exercise. Never paste API keys into prompts or saved evidence.

tools.name: Google AI Studio
tools.skill: Test a pretrained hosted vision model on unseen images, without pretending you trained it.
tools.setup: Use your own Google account and an eligible free-tier project/model. Verify its image-input support and data-use terms before uploading.
tools.assignment: Photograph an apple and orange you own against two backgrounds. Reserve the second background as a held-out test. Ask for labels with an unknown option, then record correct, incorrect and uncertain cases.
tools.caution: This is pretrained inference, not custom training. Free-tier inputs may be used to improve products. Image generation and every model are not automatically free.

tools.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
tools.skill: Explore a hosted inference request and the limits of automatic moderation.
tools.setup: Create your own Cloudflare account. Check the current Workers AI allocation and choose a supported text model in the dashboard playground, if available. Do not deploy another service just for this exercise.
tools.assignment: Write your moderation rules before testing the fictional comments. Run the sample prompt, compare every label to a human review, and identify a false positive or borderline case.
tools.caution: A free inference allowance is not unlimited hosting or access to every model. If a dashboard test is unavailable or requests billing, use the manual fixture or Groq route instead.

tools.name: Claude
tools.skill: Extract evidence from a document without inventing figures, periods or percentages.
tools.setup: Use free chat and the supplied fictional PDF if attachments are available. Otherwise paste one short page of the supplied text. No Projects or API subscription is required.
tools.assignment: Extract values with page numbers, period, currency and scope. Open the original fixture and check every row. Omit percentage changes when the two periods are not comparable.
tools.caution: Free chat is not a free Claude API entitlement. Upload limits and features vary. Use the fictional fixture, not confidential reports.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.skill: Build an instruction-bounded editor in an ordinary chat.
tools.setup: Open a fresh free chat. Paste the provided editor instructions as a user message; you do not need a custom-GPT builder or paid API.
tools.assignment: Test a messy sentence, an already correct sentence, and a request to ignore the editing rules. Count the requested items and log one boundary failure or uncertainty.
tools.caution: Persona prompting is not model fine-tuning and a chat instruction is not a privileged system message. Following one test does not prove enforcement.

tools.name: Hugging Face Spaces
tools.skill: Compare hosted model outputs while controlling the task and settings.
tools.setup: Choose a working server-backed image Space with a model card, usage/license information and an explicit no-charge route. Inspect its source or documentation; skip browser-model downloads.
tools.assignment: Keep the scene and aspect ratio fixed. Change only one style modifier for three runs. Save the model/version, prompt, settings, output and an observation about content drift.
tools.caution: A Space is not automatically free, hosted inference or safe for private inputs. Some sleep, queue, charge, or execute models in your browser. If hosted execution cannot be verified, use another hosted image tool or inspect the manual example.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.skill: Turn vague logo feedback into a controlled revision and test.
tools.setup: Create an Adobe account. Confirm a free generation is available for the selected model and feature. Start with text-to-image rather than assuming every editor feature is included.
tools.assignment: Generate a fictional logo, revise exactly two constraints, and compare legibility at a small size. Keep both prompts and note unwanted elements that remain.
tools.caution: Availability, credits, models and licensing differ. Do not promise trademark clearance or identical reruns. Never pay just to complete this practice; use the supplied design route if blocked.

tools.name: Canva
tools.access: Free editor · AI features may be paid
tools.skill: Judge composition using an actual occupied-area check, not just an AI adjective.
tools.setup: Open the free editor and use your own photo or a free asset. Use an AI generation feature only if your account explicitly includes a no-charge allowance.
tools.assignment: Make two layouts with the object occupying about 5% and 25% of the canvas. If eligible, generate an AI alternative with the prompt. Compare measured bounds and label each artifact as manual design or hosted generation.
tools.caution: Magic Expand is not assumed free. Free editing alone is not an AI run. A manual layout can prepare your test but must be recorded as design-only, not generated evidence.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.skill: Hear how voice choice and one controllable parameter affect comprehension.
tools.setup: Use a stock voice and your own short script. Check your free allowance and available controls before generating. No cloning or paid voice is needed.
tools.assignment: Generate two readings of the same short script. Change one available setting or voice, time the recordings and mark pronunciation or pacing errors. If no controls are exposed, compare two stock voices.
tools.caution: Voice cloning and commercial rights are not assumed included in the free plan. Do not imitate a real person without consent. Control names and behavior vary by model.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.access: Free basic automation · AI may require paid access
tools.skill: Separate a workflow plan from a genuinely running AI automation.
tools.setup: Start with a diagram and fictional records. Check your plan before connecting accounts. A basic trigger/action may fit free access; do not activate a trial or paid AI step to finish this exercise.
tools.assignment: Map trigger, validation, transformation, approval and action. Run the classification manually in a free text tool. If your plan supports a basic non-AI workflow, test one synthetic record; do not publish outbound messaging without approval.
tools.caution: The original email → AI → spreadsheet chain is multi-step and not promised on the free plan. A manual AI handoff is not a fully automated AI workflow. Record design-only unless you actually ran the supported chain.
